הֶ הַּ , הַ, הֲ, (on the different forms, see Ges^§ 100. 4: on Deut 32:6, see הַל),
interrogative particle (Biblical Aramaic and הֲ ᵑ7, Arabic ), prefixed, as a rule, to the first word of a sentence (or clause).
in direct questions:

as a simple interrogative, where the answer expected is uncertain, Exod 2:7 הַאֵלֵךְ shall I go and call thee a nurse ? 1Sam 23:11 הֲיַסְגִּרֻנִי will the men of Keilah deliver me into his hand ? שָׁאוּל הֲיֵרֵד will Saul come down ? Job 1:8; and frequently.

often in questions, expressed in a tone of surprise, or put rhetorically, to which a negative answer is expected (= Latin num ?): Gen 4:9 אָנֹכִי אָחִי הֲשֹׁמֵר Amos I my brother's keeper ? 18:17 shall I hide from Abraham that which I am about to do ? 30:2; 50:19; Num 11:23 a Deut 4:33 עַם֗֗֗ הֲשָׁמַע Did a people ever hear the voice of God speaking out of the midst of the fire, . . . and live ? 20:19 (read with ᵑ9 ᵑ6 ᵑ7 ᵐ5 Ew Ke Di etc. הֶאָדָם for הָאָדָם), 2Sam 7:5 בַיִת תִּבְנֶהלִּֿי ַהאַתָּה (altered in 1Chr 17:4 to the negative וג תִּבְנֶה אַתָּה ׳לֹא), 2Kin 6:22 ֗֗֗ שָׁבִיתָ הַאֲשֶׁר those whom thou hast taken captive with thy sword and with thy bow, wilt thou smite ? Isa 28:24; 36:12; a 57:6; 58:5; Jer 15:12; 16:20; Amos 5:25; Psa 50:13; Job 8:11; 15:7-8, 11; 38:12, 16, 17, 22 etc.; before an infinitive absolute (Ew^§ 328 a) Jer 7:9; Job 40:2 and probably Micah 2:7 (read הֶאָמוֺר: ). After a protasis, הִנֵההֲ֗֗֗ Num 22:38; 2Kin 7:2, 19; Jer 32:27; Ezek 17:10; after הֵן Jer 3:1; Hag 2:12: compare after זוּלַי Gen 24:5; after אִם Job 14:14 הֲיִחְיֶה גֶּבֶר יָמוּת אִם a man dieth, shall he live ? Occasionally, one or more words precede הֲ (in the same clause) for special emphasis: 2Sam 7:7; Job 34:31 הֶאָמַר אֶלאֵֿל כִּי for to God did one ever say. . .. Neh 13:27; Jer 22:15 (הֲלֹא), compare 23:26.

it is used in questions which, by seeming to make doubtful what cannot be denied, have the force of an impassioned or indignant affirmation: Gen 27:36 ('dubitantis speciem prae se fert Esavus, ut eo acerbius affirmet,' Maurer, cited by Ges), 1Sam 2:27 וגי נִגְלֵיתִי הֲנִגְלהֹ Did I reveal myself to the house of thy father, when they were in Egypt ? etc. (i.e. of course I did, although thy sons, by their actions, appear to belie it), 1Kin 16:31 (expressing astonishment), 21:19 וְגַםיָֿרָ֑שְׁתָּ הֲרָצַחְתָּ Hast thou slain, and also taken possession ? Jer 31:20; Job 20:4; 41:1 (compare Hi); also Gen 16:13, and the phrases הַרְּאִיתֶם do ye see ? 1Sam 10:24; 2Kin 6:32; הֲרָאִיתָ dost thou see ? 1Kin 20:13; Ezek 8:12, 15, 17 and elsewhere
in disjunctive questions, the first question being introduced usually by הֲ, the second by אִם or (more rarely) וְאִם: see examples under אִם

(p. 50). The disjunctive question may express a real alternative (as Josh 5:13), or (as especially in poetry) the same thought may be repeated in a different form, in two parallel clauses (e.g. Isa 10:15): in the latter case, the answer No is usually expected. Only very rarely is the second question introduced by הֲ Judg 14:15 (where, however, הֲלֹם ought no doubt to be read, with MSS., ᵑ7 Be and others, for הֲלֹא), or אוֺ 18:19; Job 16:3; 38:28, 31.
In indirect interrogation, whether (German ob. . . .?) —

singly, after verbs of seeing Gen 8:8 הֲ לִרְאוֺת to see whether, 18:21; Exod 4:18; Song 6:11, telling Gen 43:6, trying Deut 13:4, knowing Judg 3:4; Eccl 3:21 (read הַעֹלָה and הֲיֹרֶדֶת: see De or Wr on the passage.)

disjunctively, — usually אִם ֗֗֗ הֲ, Num 13:18 end, 13:19a (and see the land) ֗֗֗ רָעָה אִם הִיא הֲטוֺבָה whether it be good or bad, 13:19 b; 13:20; 13:20; לֹא אִם ֗֗֗ הֲ Gen 24:21; 27:21; 37:32; Exod 16:4 that I may try it (the people) לֹא אִם בְּתוֺרָתִי הֲיֵלֵךְ whether it will walk in my law or not, Num 11:23; Deut 8:2; Judg 2:22; הֲ ֗֗֗ הֲ Num 13:18 (by side of אִם ֗֗֗ הֲ); אוֺ ֗֗֗ הֲ Eccl 2:19; 11:6. It is prefixed to other particles, as הֲלֹא הֲכִי, הֲגַם, הַאַף, הַאִם,: see אַף אִם,,etc. p. 49, etc.
ו
ו, Waw, sixth letter; in modern Hebrew = numeral 6; no evidence of this usage in OT times.
demonstrative adverb and

conjunction so, then, and (Phoenician, Moabite, Aramaic ו; Arabic ; Ethiopic Assyrian u Dl^W (but between verbs the usually connective is the enclitic ma KAT^2. 508, Dl^§§ 82, 150). The use in Hebrew shews that original וְ was not a merely copulative conjunction, but that it possessed a demonstrative force (compare Dr^§ 122), which is often perceptible as such, though in other cases, from its being applied to denote mere juxtaposition or connection [compare Greek τε, and Latin tum .... tum = 'both .... and,' both properly demonstratives: Assyrian ma has also a demonstrative force, Dl^§ 79], it is less palpable) — וְ before shwa' mobile or a labial is vocalized וּ; often before a tone-syll., when the word itself has a disj. accent, וָ (as וַָמתִּי׃ Gen 19:19; וָמֵ֖תוּ 33:13; וָמֵ֑ת 44:9; וָחָֽיָה׃ Exod 1:16; וָיָ֑מָּה Josh 15:46; וָ֔לֹ֕א 2Sam 13:26; וָאָ֖רֶץ Isa 26:19; וָקָ֔מוּ 49:7; וָחָֽתָּה׃ Jer 48:1; וָרָֹע Psa 10:15); especially when it forms with the preceding word a pair, whether of parallel or opposed ideas (as וָכֹה כֹּה Exod 2:12, וָמִ֖י מִי 10:8, וָאָ֑בֶן אֶבֶן Deut 25:13; וָדֹ֑ר דֹּר 32:7 +; וָבֹ֔הוּ תֹּהוּ Gen 1:2, וָרֶמֶ֛שׂ בְּהֵמָה 1:24, וָרָֽע׃ טוֺב 2:19, וָנָ֖ד נָע 4:12, וָלָ֖יְלָה וְיוֺם וָחֹ֛רֶף וְקַיִץ 8:22, וֵָלךְ׃ קַח 12:19, וָאָֽרֶץ׃ שָׁמַיִם 14:19, וָאָ֑תָּה אֲנִי 31:44, וָה֑וּא אֲנִי 41:11, וָשׁוּבוּ עִבְרוּ Exod 32:27, וָהֵ֛ם אַתָּה Num 16:16, וָמֶ֑לָךְ אֱלֹהִים 1Kin 21:13, וָנֶ֖כֶד נִין Isa 14:22, וָשֶׁ֖בֶר שֹׁד 59:7; and often: see more fully Bö^§ 600); occasionally also with a conjunctive accent (as לְעֹלָֽם׃ וָשַחי Gen 3:22 compare Lev 18:5, שָׁם וָמַ֣תְנוּ 2Kin 7:4, חֲדָשָׁ֑ה וָאָ֣רֶץ Isa 65:17; Prov 25:3, גָּדוֺל׃ וָשֶשׁבֶר שֹׁ֖ד Jer 48:3, compare 32:29). — וְ is used very freely and widely in Hebrew, but also with much delicacy, to express relations and shades of meaning which Western languages would usually indicate by distinct particles. But in Hebrew particles such as לָכֵן לְמַעַן, בַּעֲבוּר, אוּלָם, אָכֵן, אַךְ, אָז, אוֺ,, etc., were reserved for cases in which special emphasis or distinctness was desired: their frequent use was felt instinctively to be inconsistent with the lightness and grace of movement which the Hebrew ear loved; and thus in AV, RV, words like or, then, but, notwithstanding, howbeit, so, thus, therefore, that, constantly appear, where the Hebrew has simply וְ.

And, connecting both words (see above), and sentences (Gen 1:5 וג קָרָא ׳וְלַחשֶׁךְ). When three, four, or more words follow, the conjunction may connect them all, as 7:21; 10:2 (6 t.) 24:35 (7 t.) Josh 7:24 (10 t.) 2Sam 17:28f.: often however it is prefixed only to the last, as Gen 5:32; 10:1; Deut 18:10 etc.; occas. even it connects only the first two, 1Kin 8:47; Isa 1:13; Psa 45:9; Job 42:9. Remarkably, however, וְ as a mere conjunction is, as a rule, not in classical Hebrew attached directly to verbs (especially in the perfect), the construction with וְ consecutive (see

2) being (as in Moabite) preferred: thus וַיִּבֶן יָצָא is said, not וּבָנָה יָצָא. Exceptions in classical Hebrew are (a) sometimes where synonyms are coupled, as Num 23:19 וְדִבֶּר ֗֗֗ אָמַר, Deut 2:30; Judg 5:26; 1Sam 12:2; Isa 1:2 ורוממתי גדּלתי 2:11; 5:14; 8:8; 19:6; 29:20; (b) isolated cases, difficult to reduce to rule (perhaps sometimes due to textual error), as Gen 28:6; 38:5; Judg 3:23; 7:13; 16:18; 1Sam 1:12; 3:13; 4:19; 5:7; 10:9; 17:38, 48; 25:20 and elsewhere (in other passages, apparently similar, the perfect and וְ has a frequent. force (see 2), as Gen 37:3; Exod 36:29f.; Num 10:17f. 21:15, 20; 1Sam 2:22; 16:14; 17:34f. (see Dr) 27:9; 2Sam 16:13; 17:17, perhaps also Gen 15:6; 21:25; 34:5). In later parts of OT, probably through Aramaic influence, the perfect with simple וְ occurs more frequently: so especially in Ecclesiastes, where it is all but universal (e.g. 2:11-12, 13, 15 etc.). With the imperfect, the simple וְ is not so unidiomatic, even in classical Hebrew (compare 3); see 1:9, 26; 9:27; 17:2; 22:17; 27:29; Exod 23:8 (frequently) 24:7; Num 14:12; Deut 17:13; 30:12-13, Josh 3:13; 7:3; Judg 7:3; 13:8; Isa 5:29; 14:10; often also in Jeremiah, Isa^2, Job, Psalms, e.g. 40:30; 41:20 (Dr^§ 116: contrast 28:13). See more fully Dr^§ 130-4 Ges^§ 112. 6. Special senses: —
it sometimes = and specially, Gen 3:16; 1Kin 11:1 many strange women, and specially the daughter of Pharaoh, Isa 1:1 Judah and (= and particularly) Jerusalem, 2:1; 9:7; Psa 18:1.

and in particular ('und zwar'), and that (explicative), Gen 4:4; Judg 7:22; 1Sam 17:40 וּבַיַּלְקוּט, 28:3 in Ramah, and that in his city (unusual: text suspicious), 2Sam 13:20 וְשֹׁמֵמָה and that desolate, Isa 57:11 I have been silent וּמֵעוֺלָם and that from of old, 32:7; Jer 15:13; Amos 3:11 (si vera lectio), 4:10; Zech 9:9b Mal 1:11; Psa 68:10; Prov 3:12; Lam 3:26; Eccl 8:2; Dan 1:3; 8:10; 9:25, 27; Neh 8:13; 1Chr 9:27; 2Chr 8:13; 29:27 (but' even' for ו, before ל and infinitive, e.g. in Isa 44:28; Jer 17:10; 19:12, is wrong; see Ew^§ 351 c, Dr^§ 206).

sometimes it introduces an idea which so exceeds or adds to what has preceded, that it is nearly equivalent to also, 1Sam 25:43; 1Kin 2:22 ask also the kingdom for him; unusually Hosea 8:6 והוא מישׂראל כי for of Israel is it also, Eccl 5:6 והבלים (see De) 2Chr 27:5 (but see ᵐ5). Or it may be rendered yea: so especially in the ascending numerations 3-4 Amos 1:3, 6, 9, 11, 13; 2:1, 4, 6; Prov 30:18, 21, 29, 6-7 6:16; Job 5:19, 7-8 Micah 5:4 — the first number being aggravated, or augmented, by a higher. In one idiom וּגְבוּל, occurring in geographic descriptions, it is used peculiarly, seemingly = at the same time: Num 34:6 and as for the western border, וּגְבוּל הַגָּדוֺל הַיָּם לָכֶם וְהָיָה the great sea shall be to you also (German 'zugleich') a border, Deut 3:16 וּגְבוּל הַנַּחַל תּוֺךְ the middle of the stream being at the same time the border, 3:17; Josh 13:23, 27; 15:12, 47 (but these, except Num 34:6, might be cases of 5c γ).

it connects alternative cases, so that it = or: Exod 20:10, 17; 21:16 he that stealeth a man בְיָדוֺ וְנִמְצָא וּמְכָרוֺ and selleth him, and (= or if) he be found in his hand, 21:17; Lev 21:14; 22:23-24, Prov 29:9 (Fl Ew RV: whether . . . or) Job 31:13, 16, 26, etc.

it connects contrasted ideas, where in our idiom the contrast would be expressed explicitly by but; in such cases prominence is usually given to the contrasted idea by its being placed immediately after the conjunction: Gen 2:17 but of the tree of the knowledge . . . thou shalt not eat, 4:2, 5; 6:8; 17:21; 31:10 etc., 1Kin 2:26; 10:7; 11:32, 34; 15:14; Prov 10:1-2, 3, 4 + often; even after לֹא (where כִּי or אִם כִּי might be expected), as Gen 42:10; Exod 21:18; Lev 26:45; Deut 11:11; Judg 19:12; 1Kin 3:11.

it introduces a contrasted idea in such a way as to suggest a question, especially before a pronoun, Judg 14:16 I told it not to my father or my mother, אַגִּיד וְלָךְ and shall I told it unto thee? 2Sam 11:11; Jer 25:29 תִנָּקוּ הִנָּקֵה וְאַתֶּם and shall ye be guiltless? 45:5; Ezek 20:31; 33:25b Jonah 4:11. So the וְ consecutive and perfect (see 2a), Exod 5:5 וְהִשְׁבַּתֶּם and will ye make them rest from their burdens? Num 16:10 וּבִקַּשְׁתֶּם and seek ye the priesthood also? 1Sam 25:11; Isa 66:9; Psa 50:21 and shall I keep silence? Job 32:16 (compare Dr^§ 119 γ).

attaching a fresh subj. (or object) to a clause already grammatically complete, it = and also, Gen 2:9b Num 16:2, 18 and they stood at the entrance of the tent of meeting, ואהרן ומשׁה and Moses and Aaron (stood also), 16:27; Exod 35:22; Judg 6:5; Gen 1:16; b 12:17; 44:2; 46:15; Exod 29:3; Jer 32:29 (compare Dr^Sm. i. 6, 11, & p. 293): when the idea thus attached is subordinate, or not logically embraced in the principal predicate, it approximates to the Arabic or 'waw of association' (followed by an accusative: W^AG ii. § 37), Est 4:16 אָצוּם וְנַעֲרֹתַי אֲנִי I will fast (singular) and (= with) my maidens, Exod 21:4; 1Sam 25:42; 29:10b (but insert here אַתָּה with ᵐ5) 2Sam 12:30 (but read וּבָהּ, as 1Chr 20:2) 1Sam 20:10; Neh 6:12; Gen 4:20; Isa 42:5; Jer 19:1 (but read מזקני וְלָקַחְתָּ֫ with ᵐ5) 2Chr 2:3; 13:11; compare Jer 22:7 (וְכֵלָיו אִישׁ), Job 41:12. Whether Isa 48:16 וְרוּחוֺ belongs here, is dubious

וְ repeated = both . . . and (but גַּם ֗֗֗ גַּם) is more usual in this sense); Gen 34:28; Num 9:14; Josh 9:23; 2Sam 5:8 (text dubious), Isa 16:5; 38:15; Jer 13:14; 21:6; 32:14 (text dubious) 32:20; 40:8; Psa 76:7; Job 34:29; Dan 8:13; Neh 12:28.

a repetition of the same word with וְ interposed expresses (a) diversity (rare), Deut 25:13 וָאֶבֶן אֶבֶן a weight and a weight, i.e. different weights (explained by וּקְטַנָּה גְּדֹלָה), 25:14; Prov 20:23; Psa 12:3 וָלֵב בְּלֵב with a heart and a heart = with a double heart, 1Chr 12:33 וָלֵב לֵב בְּלֹא; (b) distribution (except in וָדֹר דֹּר Deut 32:7; Isa 13:20 +?^Intr. 505) Psa 87:5; 1Chr 26:13 וָשָֽׁעַר׃ לְשַׁעַר = for every gate, 28:14 (twice in verse); 2Chr 8:14; 34:13; 35:15; Ezra 10:14 וָעִיר עִיר זִקְנֵי elders of every city, Neh 13:24; Est 1:8, 22 (twice in verse); 2:12; 3:4, 12 (4 t. in verse); 8:9 (twice in verse); strengthened by כָּלֿ2Chr 11:12 ועיר עיר בכל in every several city, 19:5; 28:25; 31:19; 32:28; Est 2:11 ויום בכליֿום, 3:14; 4:3; 8:11, 13, 17 (twice in verse); 9:21, 27, 28; Psalm 45:18; Psa 145:13 (common in post-Biblical Hebrew, especially with כל).

it is used in the formulation of proverbs (the Vav adaequationis, הִשְׁתַּוָּאָה וָו) as Prov 17:3; 25:3, 20, 25 cold waters to a thirsty soul and good news from a far country (i.e. they are like each other), 26:3, 9, 14, 20; 27:21; Eccl 5:2; 7:1; 8:8; compare 9:11; Psa 19:5; 125:2; Job 14:11f.; 14:19 (compare in Arabic 'every man and his cares [accusative],' 'every thing and its price,' i.e. they go together: 'merchants and dogs [accusative] of Seleucia,' i.e. they are like one another: see Fl^Kl. Schr. iii. 535 f.). More rarely in the opposite order, 5:7; 12:11. But 1Sam 12:15b cannot be thus explained: read with וּבְמַלְכְּכֶם ᵐ5, and see Dr.

in circumstantial clauses וְ introduces a statement of the concomitant conditions under which the action denoted by the principal verb takes place: in such cases, the relation expressed by וְ must often in English be stated explicitly by a conjunction, as when, since, seeing, though, etc., as occasion may require. So very often, as Gen 11:4 let us build a tower בַשָּׁמַיִם וְראֹשׁוֺ and its top in the heavens (= with its top in etc.), 18:12 shall I have pleasure, זָקֵן וַאדֹנִי and my lord is old (= my lord being old)? Judg 16:15 How sayest thou, I love thee, אִתִּי אֵין וְלִבְּךָ and (= when) thy heart is not with me? and especially with a person pronoun, Gen 15:2 what wilt thou give me עֲרִירִי הֹלֵךְ וְאָנֹכִי and I (= the case being that I) am going hence childless? 18:13; 20:3 lo, thou wilt die because of the woman thou hast taken בָּֽעַל׃ בְּעֻלַת וְהִוא = seeing she is married, 24:62 ישֵׁב וְהוּא = since or for he was dwelling (different from וַיֵּשֶׁב = and he proceeded to dwell), 26:27 וְאַתֶּם seeing ye hate me, Judg 13:9 and came to her ישֶׁבֶת וְהִיא = as she was sitting, 1Sam 18:23; 1Kin 19:19 +? Psa 72:12 the afflicted לוֺ וְאֵיןעֹֿזֵר and (= when) he has no helper (compare Job 29:12), Job 104:25 מִסְמָּר וְאֵין, Job 105:34; 5:9. See more fully Dr^§ 156-60 Ges^§ 141, R 2. (The analogous use of the is very common in Arabic: W^ii. § 183.) Introducing an appeal to a fact confirmatory of some statement or promise, it almost = as truly as (compare Ew^§ 340 c) Hosea 12:6 and J. is God of hosts, J. is his name! Joel 4:20; Amos 9:5-6 Isa 51:15 and I [who promise this] am J. thy God, who . . . . ! Jer 29:23; Psa 89:38b (compare in Qoran the frequently 'And God is .. . . . [the mighty, the merciful, etc.]').
The ו consecutive (formerly called the Waw 'conversive'); —
with the
imperfect (וַּ with following daghesh; before וָ א,), as וַיּאֹמֶר properly = and he proceeded to say, chiefly in contin. of a preceding perfect tense (so Moabite);
with the

perfect (וְ, — in 1 & 2 singular, the tone, with certain exceptions [see Dr^§ 110], being thrown forward to the ultima), as וְיָָֽשַׁבְתָּ֫ properly so [namely, as limited by a verb, or other term, preceding] hadst thou sat, chiefly in continuation of a preceding imperfect tense, in its various senses of future, jussive, or frequentative. Thefurther analysis of these idioms belongs to the grammar; see on a Dr^Ch. vi., Ges^§ 111, and on

b Dr^Ch. viii. Ges^§ 112. Here it must suffice to note — (a) ו consecutive (especially with the imperfect) frequently couples two verbs in such a manner that the first, indicating the general character of the action, receives its closer definition in the second: in such cases, the first may often be represented in English by an adverb, as Gen 26:18 וַיַּחְמֹּר וַיָּשָׁב and he turned and dug = and he dug again; so often; and similarly with הוֺסִיף 25:1, מִהַר 24:18, הוֺאִיל Josh 7:7, etc.; more exceptionally, Gen 30:27; Est 8:6, and (not consecutive) Gen 47:6; Job 23:3; Song 2:3; Lam 3:26 (see Ges^§ 120, 2 a; compare in Syriac Nö^§ 335-6. In Arabic the stronger form of the conjugation here corresponds: W^ii. § 140). (b) וַּ with the imperfect sometimes expresses a contrast = and yet, Gen 32:31 I have seen God face to face וַתִּנָּצֵל and yet my soul is delivered, Deut 4:33; 2Sam 3:8; 19:29; Isa 51:12; Psa 73:14; 144:3; Job 10:8 + (compare Dr^§ 74 β). (c) there is a tendency in the later books of the OT to use the perfect with simple וְ, where the classical language would employ the imperfect with וַּ (compare above

1); so especially in Ecclesiastes, where וַּ occurs thrice only, Job 1:17; 4:1, 7. (d) a double perfect with ו consecutive is sometimes used, informally but neatly, with a hypothetical force; thus (a) in past or present time Exod 16:21 וְנָמָֽס׃ הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ וְחַם and the sun used to be warm, and it used to melt = and if (or when) the sun was warm, it melted, 33:10; 1Kin 18:10; Jer 18:4, 8 וְנִחַמְתִּ֫י וְֹשָׁב = and if it turns, I repent, 20:9 (see RV); (β) in future time, Gen 44:22 ומת אביו ועזב and he will leave his father, and he will die = and if he leaves his father, he will die, 33:13; 42:38; Exod 4:14; 12:13; 1Sam 16:2; 19:3; Ezek 33:3; 39:15 etc. (Dr^§ 147-9, Ges^§ 159. 2 e).
With a

voluntative (cohortative or jussive) וְ expresses an intention, that or so that (an elegancy by which the too frequent use of לְמַעַן or בַּעֲבוּר is avoided): Exod 10:17 entreat God, וְיָסֵר so may he remove (= that he may remove) this death, Gen 27:4 and bring it me וְאֹכֵ֑לָה so let me eat (= that I may eat); and without the modal form being externally indicated, Exod 14:1 speak . . . וְיָשֻׁבוּ that they return, 14:15; and often Sts. even of past time, as 1Kin 13:33 whom he would, he consecrated וִיהִי that there might be priests of the high places, 2Kin 19:25; Isa 25:9 a Lam 1:19. After a negative, Psa 51:18 thou desirest not sacrifice, וְאֶתֵּ֑נָה so [= in that case] would I give it (or, that I might give it), 55:13 וְאֶשָּׂא so could I bear it (or, that I might bear it), Isa 53:2 RVm Num 23:19; Jer 5:28 RV. Sts. also before an imperative, Gen 12:2 and be (= that thou mayest be) a blessing, 2Sam 21:3 +. See more fully Dr^§ 59-65, Ges^§ 108. 2; 109. 2; 110. 2. (In Arabic with the subjunctive is used similarly: W^ii. § 15 d.) A volunt. is also sometimes attached by וְ to a preceding volunt. or imperative, so as to form a virtually hypothetical sentence, as Gen 42:18 וִחְיוּ עֲשׂוּ זֹאת = if you do this, you shall live, 30:28; 34:12; Prov 3:9f. 4:4, 8; Isa 55:2: see Dr^§ 152.

It expresses often an informal inference, or consequence, so, then, especially at the beginning of a speech: Gen 27:8; Psa 2:10 and often וְעַתָּה now, therefore; וְלָמָּה and וּמַדּוּעַ why, then? Gen 29:25; Num 12:8; 16:3 +; Exod 2:20 וְאַיּוֺ where, then, is he? Gen 34:21; 1Sam 15:14; 26:22 וְיַעֲבֹר let, then, . . . come over, 2Sam 24:3; 2Kin 4:41 קֶמַח וּקְחוּ then bring meal, Ezek 18:32. So the וְ consecutive and the perfect, as Deut 2:4 וְנִשְׁמַרְתֶּם take heed, therefore, 4:15; 7:9 וְיָָֽדַעְתָּ֫ know, therefore, 30:19; 1Sam 6:5; 1Kin 2:6; Ruth 3:9; Josh 15:19; Isa 40:6b (Dr^§ 119 δ).
ו introduces the predicate or apodosis: namely

וְ consecutive and the Perfect — in answer to אִם or כִּי constantly, as Exod 19:5; 23:22 if thou hearkenest to my voice, וְאָֽיַבְתִּ֫י then am I (= I will be) enemy to thy enemies (see Dr^§ 136-8); after the casus pendens, 12:44 every servant that is bought for money, וּמַלְתָּ֫ה thou shalt circumcise him, etc. Num 14:31; 24:24; 1Sam 25:27; 2Sam 14:10 he that spake unto thee, אֵלַי וַהֲבֵאתוֺ so hast thou brought him (= thou shalt bring him) unto me, Isa 9:4; 56:6f. +; Exod 12:15; 31:14; Deut 17:12 +; after various time-determinations, as Gen 3:5 in the day of your eating from it וְנִפְקְחוּ then shall your eyes be opened, Exod 16:6 וִידַעְתֶּם עֶרֶב at even, then shall ye know, 16:7; 32:34; 2Sam 15:10; 1Kin 13:31 אֹתִי וּקְבַרְתֶּם בְּמוֺתִי when I die, so ye shall bury me, etc., + often; after conjs., as כִּי Gen 29:15, יַעַן 1Kin 20:28; Isa 3:16f., תַּחַת 60:15, etc., (see Dr^§ 123).

וַּ consecutive and the imperfect (but much less frequently than the perfect), as Gen 30:30 the little that thou hadst, וַיִּפְרֹץ it hath increased, Exod 9:21; 2Sam 4:10; 1Kin 9:20f. 15:13 +; after time-determinations, Gen 22:4 on the third day וַיִּשָּׂא then Abraham lifted up his eyes, 19:15; 27:34; 37:18; 1Sam 6:6; 12:8; Isa 6:1; Hosea 11:1 when Israel was a child, וָאֹהֲבֵהוּ then I loved him, +; occasionally after conjunctions, as כַּאֲשֶׁר Exod 16:34, יַעַן 1Sam 15:23, לְמַעַן Isa 45:4, אִם Psa 59:16 (Dr^§ 127).

in other cases (not 'consecutive') — all more or less uncommon: namely a. וְ closely joined to the imperfect Gen 13:9 if to the left, וְאֵימִינָה then I will take the right (compare 2Sam 12:8) Exod 12:3 on the 10th of the month וְיִקְחוּ then let them take, Num 16:5; Isa 43:4; Hosea 4:6; 10:10; Psa 69:33; Job 15:17; 2Sam 22:41; Prov 23:24 Kt (Dr^§ 125); β. separated from the verb, Exod 8:22; Lev 7:16 יֵאָכֵל וְהַנּוֺתָר וּמִמָּחֳרָת and on the morrow, then the remainder shall be eaten, Josh 3:3; 1Kin 8:32; Isa 8:7; 48:7; Job 14:7; 20:18; b 23:12; 25:5; 32:14 +; γ. without a verb, Gen 40:9 וְהִנֵּה בַּחֲלֹמִי in my dream, behold, a vine was before me, 40:16; 2Sam 23:3f.; Prov 10:25, and the extreme cases 2Sam 15:34 thy father's slave, מֵאָז וַאֲנִי I was that of old, — but now עַבְדְּךָ וַאֲנִי well, I will be thine, Isa 34:12 (si vera lectio), Job 4:6b דְּרָכֶיךָ וְתֹם תִּקְוָָֽתְךָ thy confidence — it is the uprightness of thy ways, 36:26 חֵקֶר וְלֹא שָׁנָיו מִסְמַּר Ges. seine Jahre, da ist kein Zählen (compare Dr^§ 124-5, 128-9). — With 4, 5 compare the Arabic , W^i. § 366 b, 367 c; ii. § 187; Dr^§ 185 end.
the, He, fifth letter; = numeral 5 in post-Biblical Hebrew; no evidence of this usage in OT times.
הֶ הָ, הַ, , הַּ (on the use of these different forms, see the Grammars: e.g. Ges^§ 35),

definite article, the (so Moabite, Phoenician (Schröd^§ 62-4), Liµyan (Northwest Arabia) ha (DHM^Epigr. Denkm. 4. 13. 58 ff.); not Assyrian Aramaic or Ethiopic: Arabic , of which, before dentals, sibilants, and liquids, the l is written but not pronounced, thus pronounced 'ash-shamsu = Hebrew הַשֶּׁמֶשׁ) — in General the use of the article in Hebrew is analogous to its use in Greek or German: but naturally there are applications peculiar to Hebrew (compare with what follows Ges^§ 126 Ew^§ 277): —
joined with substantives:

to mark a definite concrete object, as Gen 1:1 the heavens and the earth, הַמֶּלֶךְ the king, etc. Never, however (as in Greek e.g. ὁ Πλάτων), before true proper names, though it is used with certain terms, chiefly geographical, of which the original appellative sense has not been lost, as הַבַּעַל 'Baal,' literally 'the lord,' in plural הַבְּעָלִים i.e. the various local Baals, הַשָּׂטָן the Adversary Job 1:6ff. (as a proper name שָׂטָן, 'Satan,' only 1Chr 21:1); הַלְּבָנוֺן (but not הַחֶרְמוֺן), הַיַּרְדֵּן (but not הָאַרְנֹן), הַשָּׁרוֺן הַכַּרְמֶל, the Sharon, הַשְּׁפֵלָה the (Judaean) lowland, הַמִּישׁוֺר הַכִּכָּר, the (Moabite) table-land, הָעַי הָעֲרָבָה, '`Ai,' הַגִּבְעָה 'Gibeah,' Judg 20:5ff., הַגָּלִיל 'Galilee,' הַגִּלְעָד הַבָּשָׁן, הַגִּלְבֹּעַ, הַגִּלְגָּל, (often), הַמִּסְגָּה הָעֹפֶל, הַיְשִׁימוֺן, הָרָמָה, הַמִּצְמָּה, הַשִּׁטִּים,.

with an adjective to denote one who exhibits a quality κατ’ ἐξοχήν, i.e. to express the comparative or superlative degree: so often, as Gen 1:16 הגדל המאור the greater light, הקטן המאור the lesser light, 27:1 הגדול בנו = his elder son, 48:14 הצעיר the younger, 42:13 הַקָּטֹן the little one, i.e. the youngest, (of Joseph's brethren), Lev 21:10 מֵאֶחָיו הַגָּדוֺל the chiefest of his brethren, Num 35:25 + הגדול הכהן the chief priest, ב ׳הצעיר the least among Judg 6:15, מן הצעירה the least of 1Sam 9:21, ב ׳הַיָּפָה the fairest among Song 1:8; 2Kin 10:3; Prov 30:30, compare Job 14:15.

with nouns which are not definite in themselves, but acquire their definition from the context, or from the manner in which they are introduced: thus (α) in the standing phrases הַיּוֺם to-day, Gen 4:14; 21:26 + often; הַלַּיְלָה to-night, 19:5; 30:15 +, once 1Sam 15:16 last night; so הַשָּׁנָה this year, 2Kin 19:29; Jer 28:16; הַמַּעַם this time, Gen 18:32 +. (β) הַנָּהָר the river (κατ’ ἐξοχήν), i.e. the Euphrates; Exod 2:15 the well, the well namely of the district, Josh 8:11 the valley, 1Sam 17:3; 19:10 the wall, 19:13 the bed, 20:21 הַנַּעַר the lad (whom Jonathan would naturally take with him), 20:34 the table. Hence occas. where a suffix would define the noun more precisely, as הַחֲמוֺר 2Sam 19:27 + = my ass, Judg 3:20; 1Sam 1:9 הַכִּסֵּא = his seat, Judg 4:15; 1Kin 22:35; 2Kin 10:15 + הַמֶּרְכָּבָה, 1Sam 18:10; 20:33 הַחֲנִית.

it is a peculiarity of Hebrew thought to conceive an object as defined by its being taken for a particular purpose, and thus by a kind of prolepsis to prefix the article to the noun denoting it: 1Sam 10:1 and Samuel took הַשֶּׁמֶן אֶתמַּֿךְ literally the cruse of oil, not, however, a cruse which had been defined previously, but one rendered definiteby being now taken; in English idiom 'a cruse of oil,' 10:25 בַּסֵּפֶר literally in the scroll or book, the one, namely taken for the purpose, i.e. in a scroll (so Exod 17:14; Num 5:23; Job 19:23), 21:10 בַּשִּׂמְלָה, Judg 4:18 בַּשְּׂמִיכָה וַתְּכַסֵּהוּ, 4:19; 7:13 הָאֹהֶל a tent, 8:25; 9:48 אֶתהַֿקַּרְדֻּמֹּת hatchets, 20:16 every one able to sling אֶלהַֿשַּׂעֲרָה בָּאֶבֶן with a stone at a hair, 1Sam 6:8 בָּאַרְגָּז (unless indeed the אַרְגָּז was an understood appendage in every cart), Num 11:27 הַנַּעַר, a young man, 13:23 בַּמּוֺט on a pole, Josh 2:15 בַּחֶבֶל with a cord, 2Sam 17:17 השׁפחה a girl (compare Dr^1Sam 1:4; 19:13). Sometimes it is uncertain whether an article is to be referred to c or
d: e.g. 1Sam 2:13 his prong or a prong, 2Sam 18:9 his mule or a mule, etc.

with nouns that denote objects or classes of objects that are known to all, as הַמַּיִם הַזָּהָב, הַצּאֹן,; Gen 13:2 Abram was very rich וּבַזָּהָב בַּכֶּסֶף בַּמִּקְנֶה, Exod 31:4 וּבַכֶּסֶף בַּזָּהָב לַעֲשׂוֺת, Deut 14:26 and thou shalt lay out the money וּבַשֵּׁכָר וּבַיַּיִן וּבַצּאֹן בַּבָּקָר, 2Kin 9:30 עֵינֶיהָ בַּמּוּךְ וַתָּשֶׂם, in French 'elle mit du fard à ses yeux.' It is, however, remarkable that this usage depends mostly on the punctuation, הַלֶּחֶם הַיַּיִן, הַכֶּסֶף, etc. (except as applied to denote definite quantities of gold, wine, etc., as Josh 6:24) being far less common than יַיִן כֶּסֶף, etc., but לַכֶּסֶף בַּכֶּסֶף, etc. being much more frequently than לְכֶסֶף בְּכֶסֶף, etc.: for instances in which the article forms part of the consonantal text, see Gen 6:20; 7:8 + העוף and הבהמה, Deut 8:3 הַלָּחֶם, 1Kin 5:8; 5:13; Isa 28:7 הַיַּיִן and הַשֵּׁכָר, 60:17; Ezek 15:4, 7 הָאֵשׁ, Hab 2:5; Prov 20:1; Psalm 65:14 הַצּאֹן, Song 1:11; Eccl 7:12. compare below,

in comparisons, the object compared being, as a rule, not an individual as such, but one exhibiting the characteristics of a class: Isa 1:18 כַּתּוֺלָע כַּשָּׁנִים, like scarlet, like crimson (both meant Generally), 5:24 יִהְיֶה כַּמַּק, 5:28 כַּצַּר and כַּסּוּפָה, 10:14 כַּקֵּן, 13:8 כַּיּוֺלֵדָה (as always with this word, e.g. 42:14; Psa 48:7), 11:7 כַּבָּקָר; + often (The usage is not, however, quite uniform, at least according to the punctuation: there occurs e.g. כְּקַשׁ Job 41:21; Isa 47:14; כְּאַרְיֵה Psa 7:3 and elsewhere: and we find both כַּלָּבִיא) Isa 5:29 and כְּלָבִיא Hosea 13:8; כָּאֲרִי Isa 38:13 and כַּאֲרִי Num 24:9; כַּגִּבּוֺר Isa 42:13 and כְּגבור Job 16:14; etc.) Similarly Gen 19:28 הַכִּבְשָׁן כְּקִיטֹר as the smoke of a furnace, Num 11:8, 12 אֶתהַֿיֹּנֵק הָאֹמֵן יִשָּׂא כַּאֲשֶׁר, Deut 28:29 (הָעִוֵּר), Judg 8:18b הַמֶּלֶךְ בְּנֵי כְּתֹאַר, 14:6 הַגְּדִי כְּשַׁסַּע like (a lion's) rending a kid, 16:9; 1Kin 14:15; Zech 12:10 הַיָּחִיד עַל מִסְמֵּד כְּ as mourning over an only child, 13:9 +. Where, however, the standard of comparison is not the class in General, but only a particular part of it, defined by a special epithet (whether adjective or verb), the article is naturally omitted: thus כַּמֹּץ like chaff (in General) Isa 41:15, but עֹבֵר כְּמֹץ like chaff passing away 29:5; כַּצֵּל Job 14:2, but נָטוּי כְּצֵל Psa 102:12; כַּקַּשׁ Isa 40:24, but נִדָּף כְּקַשׁ 41:2; כָּאַיָּל 35:6, but, וג על תַּעֲרֹג ׳כְּאַיָּל like a hind (that) longeth for streams of water Psa 42:2; כָּאֵשׁ Isa 9:17, but יער תבער כְּאֵשׁ like fire (that) kindleth a wood Psa 83:15; כֶעָשָׁן Isa 51:6, but מֵאֲרֻבָּה כְּעָשָׁן like smoke from a chimney Hosea 13:3: so Isa 62:1b Job 9:26; 11:16 עָֽבְרוּ כְּמַיִם like waters (that) have passed by, etc.; Deut 32:2 a כַּטַּל כַּמָּטָר,, but 32:2 b עֲלֵיעֵֿשֶׂב כִּרְבִיבִים עֲלֵידֶֿשֶׁא, כִּשְׂעִירִים. Where the article is found, although a rel. clause follows (as Psa 1:4; 49:13; Isa 61:10), this is probably to be regarded not as limiting the class of object compared, but as describing it.

prefixed to generic nouns (in the singular) it designates the class, i.e. it imparts to the noun a collective force, as Exod 1:22 כָּלהַֿבֵּן all (literally the whole of) the sons, כָּלהַֿבַּת all the daughters, Lev 17:8, 10 מִןהַֿגֵּר of the strangers, who sojourn in their midst, Num 21:7 הַגנָּחָשׁ the serpents; Gen 14:13; Ezek 24:26; 33:21 הַמָּלִיט those who escaped; Josh 6:7 + הֶחָלוּץ, v 9:13 הַמְאַסֵּף; 8:19 הָאוֺרֵב; 1Sam 13:17 הַמַּשְׁחִית; Micah 2:13; Isa 6:4 הַקּוֺרֵא the choir of criers; 1Sam 24:14 הַקַּדְמֹנִי the ancients; Eccl 7:26 אֶתהַֿאִשָּׁה woman, and often with Gentile names, as הַיְבוּסִי the Jebusites, וְהַמְּלֵתִי הַכְּרֵתִי 2Sam 8:18 and elsewhere, הַדָּנִי Judg 18:1 etc., הַלֵּוִי the Levites, Num 3:20, 18:23; Mal 2:8; Psa 135:20 +.

with nouns denoting abstract ideas, especially the names of moral qualities (compare Greek ἡ δίκη, French la justice), chiefly in two cases — (α) where the article is recognizable in the consonantal text, exceptionally, when some emphasis or definiteness is intended, as Deut 7:9 והחסד הברית שׁומר; הזה החסד 2Sam 2:5; 1Kin 3:6; והרחמים החסד את Jer 16:5 (contr. Zech 7:9); הצדק Isa 1:26; 61:3; Eccl 3:16; הַצְּדָקָה Isa 32:17 (twice in verse) (contrast 32:16) Dan 9:7 (emphatic); הַדַּעַת Hosea 4:6; הָאֱמֶת Gen 32:11 (followed by אֲשֶׁר), Isa 59:15 (contrast 59:14) Zech 8:3, 19; הָאֱמוּנָה Isa 11:5b (contr. v^a) Jer 7:28; הַחָכְמָה Job 28:12, 20; הַחַיִּים Gen 2:9 +; הָאַהֲבָה Song 2:7; 3:5; 8:4, 7; הַשֶּׁקֶר Jer 7:4, 8; 23:26; הַמָּוֶת Isa 25:8; Ruth 1:17 +; הָרֶשַׁע Psa 125:3; Eccl 3:16; הָרִשְׁעָה Zech 5:8; הַחשֶׁךְ Isa 60:2; Eccl 2:13; see also Deut 30:15, 19 (Jer 21:8), 1Kin 7:14; Jer 32:19; Mal 2:5 והשׁלום החיים, Psa 123:4; 130:4; Dan 9:9; 1Chr 29:11; 2Chr 1:12; Prov 31:30; Eccl 2:18, 17; 7:12, 19; 10:6; 11:10: but in all such cases אֱמֶת צֶדֶק, חֶסֶד,, etc. are far more common. (β) where the article depends on the punctuation, after prepositions, especially בְּ, but with much irregularity, as בַּחֶסֶד Isa 16:5; Prov 20:28 (but ׳בְּח Hosea 2:21; Prov 16:6), בַּצֶּדֶק 25:5 (elsewhere always ׃בְּצ ׳בִּצְדָקָה also always); בֶּאֱמֶת and בֶּאֱמוּנָה always; בַּשֶּׁקֶר Isa 28:15 (but || כָּזָב, not הַכָּזָב) Jer 5:31; 13:25; 20:6; 23:14 (בְּשֶׁקֶר 3:10; 29:9); בַּשָּׁלוֺם Psa 29:11; Job 15:21 (elsewhere בְּשָׁלוֺם); Zech 12:4 to smite וּבַעִוָּרוֺן בַּשִּׁגָּעוֺן (but Deut 28:28 וּבְעורון בְּשׁגעון), compare Gen 19:11; Deut 28:22; to enter with one בַּמִּשְׁמָּט Job 9:32; 22:4 (but בְּמשׁפט Psa 143:2), contrast also Prov 18:5; with 24:23; לַמִּשְׁמָּט Isa 59:11; Psa 9:8 (but ׳לְמ Isa 5:7; Psa 122:5); Prov 2:2; 7:4 לַחָכְמָה, (but never הַחכמה in Proverbs 1-9, or indeed in the whole book); 2:3; 7:4 לַבִּינָה, Job 39:17 בַּבִּינָה (but never הַבִּינָה); Prov 2:2-3,לַתְּבוּנָה (but הַתְּבוּנָה only 1Kin 7:14 emphatic); to perish בַּצָּמָא Judg 15:18 +; Isa 29:21 בַּתֹּהוּ, 32:19 הָעִיר תִּשְׁמַּל בַּשִּׁמְּלָה German in die Niedrigkeit sinkt die Stadt, 45:16 together they go בַכְּלִמָּה (in die Schmach), 46:2 בַּשְּׁבִי into captivity, 47:5 בַחשֶׁךְ בֹּאִי (so always: never בְחשׁך). The living language may have used the article more readily after a preposition, where it did not lengthen the word by an entire syll.; still the disparity of usage between α and β makes it not improbable that the article in β is in many cases not original but due to the punctuators.

to mark the vocative: 1Sam 17:55 הַמֶּלֶךְ חֵינֿפשׁך as thy soul liveth, O king, I do not know, 17:58 הַנַּעַר אתה מי בן Whose son art thou, lad ? 2Sam 14:4 Help, O king ! 1Kin 18:26 עֲנֵנוּ הַבַּעַל, 2Kin 9:5 הַשָּׂר אֵלֶיךָ, Isa 42:18 שְׁמָ֑עוּ הֵַחרְשִׁים, Jer 2:31 וג רְאוּ אַתֶּם ׳הַדּֿוֺר, Ezek 37:4 הַיְּבֵשׁוֺת הָעֲצָמוֺת O dry bones, Mal 3:9 כֻּלּוֺ הַגּוֺי (Dr^§ 198 Obs. 2).

N.B. In poetry, the article is frequently dispensed with before words which would naturally take it in prose: thus Psa 2:2; 2:8; 2:10 & often אֶרֶץ; 8:9; 18:10; 33:6 + שָׁמַיִם; (rarely in prose, Gen 1:8; 2:4; 1Kin 8:35); 21:2; 1Ki 45:14; 1Ki 45:16; 1Ki 61:7 and elsewhere מֶלֶךְ; 1Ki 66:6; 1Ki 72:8 + יָם; 1Ki 59:7; 1Ki 59:15 עִיר; Judg 5:2; Psa 18:44 עָם etc.; 9:6; 9:17 & often רָשָׁע; Isa 1:2, 6, 21; 3:10-11, 11:6-7, 8.
With adjectives, participles, and demonstrative pronouns (אלה זאת, זה, הם, המה, היא, הוא,): namely

(so regularly) when the substantive qualified by these words is defined by it likewise, as הגדול המלך = ὁ βασιλεὺς ὁ μέγας, Gen 2:12 ההוא הארץ, 20:1 הַזֶּה הַדָּבָר, Josh 2:3 אליך הבאים האנשׁים = οἱ ἄνδρες οἱ ἐλθόντες πρὸς σέ, Gen 13:5; 16:13; 24:65; 32:21; Judg 6:28; Isa 65:3-4, 5; 66:24; Psa 31:9. So also with adjectives & participles, if the substantive be defined by a suffix (as Deut 4:37 הַגָּדֹל בְּכֹחוֺ, 1Sam 8:14 הַטֹּבוֺת זֵיתֵיכֶם); and with a pronoun, if it be defined by a Genitive (as Deut 29:20; 1Sam 14:29; 15:14; 2Kin 6:32 הַזֶּה בֶןהַֿמְּרַצֵּחַ this son of a murderer), but not if it be defined by a suffix, as Exod 10:1 אֵלֶּה אֹתֹתַי (not הָאֵלָּה אתתי), Josh 2:14 זֶה דְבָרֵנוּ this our word (not ׳ד הַזֶּה): see Dr^§ 209 Obs. Similarly when the article with the participle has a resumptive force, Psa 33:15 (Psalm 14, he looketh forth from the place, &c.), לִבָּם יַחַד הַיֹּצֵר he that formeth, etc., 19:11 מִזָּהָב הַנֶּחֱמָדִים which (Psalm 10 b) are more desirable than gold, 49:7. (:6 b the iniquity of my aggressors surroundeth me), הַבֹּטְחִים who trust in their riches, etc., Gen 49:21; Isa 46:6; 51:20; Job 6:16 + (see Dr^§ 135. 7).

(rare) when the substantive qualified by the adjective or participle was felt to be sufficiently definite for its own article to be dispensed with, as sometimes with the word day Gen 1:31 השׁשׁי יום, 2:3 השׁביעי יום, Exod 12:15, 18; 20:10 (= Deut 5:14) Lev 19:6; 22:27: so with מָנוֺא entrance Jer 38:14, שַׁעַר Zech 14:10; חָצֵר court 1Kin 7:8, 12; Ezek 40:28 and elsewhere; also in certain phrases (peculiar to P) where the substantive is defined by כל, as Gen 1:21 הַחַיָּה כָּלנֶֿפֶשׁ all living souls, 1:28 הָרֹמֶשֶׂת כָּלחַֿיָּה all living things that creep, etc., 7:21; 9:10; Lev 11:10, 46; further in isolated cases, hardly reducible to rule, 24:10; 1Sam 12:23 הַטּוֺבָה דֶּרֶךְ, 16:23 הָרָעָה רוּחַ, 2Sam 12:4 העשׁיר לְאישׁ Jer 6:20; 17:2; Zech 4:7; Psa 104:18; Ezra 10:9 הַתְּשִׁיעִי חֹדֶשׁ (quite exceptional in OT). (With pronouns this use is so rare that, where it occurs, it is dubious if the text be sound: 1Sam 17:12, 17; Jer 40:3 Kt Micah 7:11). And with the participle: 1Sam 25:10 הַמִּתְמָּֽרְצִים עֲבָדִים רַבִּים many are the slaves who break away etc., Isa 7:20; Jer 27:3; 46:16 = 50:16 הַיּוֺנָה חֶרֶב the oppressing sword, Ezek 2:3 (but ᵐ5 Co omit הגוים), 14:22; 32:22, 24; Psa 62:4; Prov 26:18; Judg 21:19 (very anomalous, read probably לַמְּסִלָּה). This usage is somewhat more frequently in the later parts of OT; and in Post-Biblical Hebrew it is very General (e.g. הָרַע יֵצֶד the evil inclination): see further Dr^§ 209.

with the participle, where the participle with the article forms really the subject: Gen 2:11 הַסּוֺבֵב הוּא not 'it was encompassing,' but 'it is that which encompassed,' 45:12 הַמְדַבֵּר מִּי my mouth is that which speaketh, Deut 3:21 הָראֹוֺת עֵינֶיךָ thine eyes were those which saw, 4:3; 8:18 ὅτι οὗτος ἐστιν ὁ διδοὺς σοί, Isa 14:27; 66:9 (see Dr^§ 135. 7).

The article is prefixed exceptionally — mostly in the latest Hebrew — with the force of a relative to the verb: Josh 10:24 אִתּוֺ הֶהָֽלְכוּא that went with him, Ezek 26:17, הַהֻ֫לָּלָה הָעִיר, 1Chr 26:28 שְׁמוּאֵל הַהִקְדִּישׁ וְכֹל and all that Samuel had dedicated, 29:8, 17; 2Chr 1:4 ַבּהֵכִין in (the place) that he had prepared, 29:36; Ezra 8:25; 10:14, 17. According to the punctuation, it occurs similarly elsewhere, as Gen 18:21 הַשָבּאָה (so 46:27; Job 2:11), 21:3 הַנּוֺלַדלֿוֺ, 1Kin 11:9 & Dan 8:1 הַנִּרְאָה, Isa 51:10 הַשָּׂ֨מָה֨, 56:3 הַנִּלְוָה, Ruth 1:22; 2:6; 4:3 (all הַשָּׁ֫בָה): but in all these passages, the change of a point, or even sometimes of an accent, would restore the normal participial construction (as לוֺ הַנּוֺלָד הַבָּשָאה, compare Gen 48:5, הַנִּרְאֶה), which is, no doubt, what was intended by the original writers, and is recognised elsewhere by the Masora, e.g. 12:7; 35:1 הַנִּרְאֶה, 46:26 & Ruth 4:11 הַבָּאָ֣ה (compare Ew^§ 331 b Ges^138, 3 b). Once, still more anomalously, before a preposition 1Sam 9:24 וְהֶעָלֶיהָ (as though καὶ τὸ ἐπ’ αὐτῆς): but read probably וְהָאַלְיָה and the fat tail, see Dr. (In Arabic also occurs, though very rarely, as a relative: W^AG i. § CG 117). — On the anomalous use of the article with a word in the stative construct, see Grammars, as Ew^§ 290 d, Ges^§ 127 R. 4, also Dr^§ 190-1.
